memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'You are to have the same law for the foreigner and the native-born. I
am the LORD your God'" - Lev 24:22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter states it once more, plainly: one law for everyone. And then
comes the reason — not sociology, not fairness as a human ideal, but
simply, "I am the LORD your God." Impartial justice flows from God's own
character.

This is worth pausing over, because Israel could easily have reasoned
otherwise. They were the covenant people. Surely there should be some
advantage? God says no. The foreigner living among them stood on the
same legal ground.

Dear reader, wherever we live, there are people who are effectively
"foreigners" among us — the migrant worker, the domestic help, the
newcomer, the person of another community or language. It costs very
little to treat such people as second class, because they rarely have
the power to object.

God notices. He repeatedly identifies Himself as the one who watches
over the foreigner (Ps 146:9) and commands His people to love the
foreigner as themselves (Lev 19:34).

In Christ, this reaches its fullest expression. Paul says there is
neither Jew nor Gentile, for we are all one in Christ Jesus (Gal 3:28).
Peter learned that God accepts people from every nation (Acts 10:34-35).
The church was never meant to be a place where some belong more than
others.

Treat the outsider well. God does.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who is treated as an outsider in my community, and how do I treat
   them?
2. Does my church genuinely welcome people unlike me?
3. What practical kindness could I show a "foreigner" this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You care for the stranger and show no partiality. Give me eyes
to see those treated as outsiders and a heart to welcome them as You
have welcomed me. Amen.
